correctness.rationale: The geometric chambers correspond to the empty set and skew-line subsets: any meeting pair of (-1)-curves has a singular principal block, and a pairwise-skew subset has matrix −I. A stable support B descends as a divisor; −K+B is nef, intersects B's components trivially, and has square 3+|B|, so −K+2B realizes the support over the ground field. Independently reconstructing incidence automorphisms from the images of an ordered skew sextuple gave 51,840 permutations, 25 classes and the stated 2,764 skew subsets. Computing the set action from this reconstruction agrees in every row with the frozen Markdown, including the fixed counts and Burnside sum 414,720. The equal line profile 3^9 does give distinct chamber profiles and counts 1 vs. 13. Over extensions they differ precisely when the degree is not divisible by three; both counts reach 2,764 at multiples of three. The cycle-power count and zeta formula follow from finite orbits.
residual_risks: The table is conditional on the given geometric Weyl class, not a field-by-field realization theorem. The two 3^9 rows do not stay distinguishable in extension degrees divisible by three.

evidence: Atkinson–van Willigenburg–Pfeiffer explicitly relate the coset action at arbitrary w to the mark indexed by its parabolic closure, and §4.4 uses the exceptional parabolic tables calculated in CHEVIE.

Rybakov–Trepalin tabulate the Weyl classes and eigenvalue types, including A2^3 and A2^2 for the two 3^9 line profiles. The TomLib definitions confirm that marks are coset fixed-point numbers; its sampled documentation alone was not used to infer a specific full group table.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The operative stronger result applies simultaneously to all eight constituent actions. The fully indexed conjugacy classes and powers specify its inputs; ordinary orbit inversion specifies the requested output. By contrast, the 27-line cycle table alone does not determine these inputs.

evidence: The all-class formula is Fix(g^n)=Σ_J β_{J,K(g^n)} for the eight constituents, with K(g^n) its parabolic closure. The requested number of d-cycles is (1/d)Σ_{e|d} Möbius(d/e)Fix(g^e). This transforms previously treated coset permutation characters directly to the claimed profiles.

The headline 1 vs. 13 can also be read from the same constituent actions: type A2^3 is elliptic and has no fixed cosets of proper parabolics. In type A2^2 (class size 480, centralizer size 108), only A5 and A2×A2×A1 among the proper stabilizers contain that class. They contain respectively 40 and 4 elements of that type, giving marks 108·40/720=6 and 108·4/72=6. The full-group constituent adds one.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The distinction between the two line-indistinguishable classes is real, but is itself a direct readout of known parabolic permutation data. This is a mathematically explicit implication, not an inference that unrelated configuration spectra must coincide or that prior wording is identical.

evidence: For a skew set S, its sum v_S has intersection −1 with precisely the members of S; all other line intersections with the sum are nonnegative. Thus Stab(S)=Stab(v_S). Subtract the canonical-class component of v_S to work in the real E6 reflection space; bringing that vector to a closed fundamental chamber identifies its stabilizer with a standard parabolic.

The eight support orbits have parabolic stabilizer types E6, D5, A4×A1, A2×A2×A1, A3×A1, A4, A4×A1, A5 (the two size-five orbits have stabilizer orders 120 and 240). All are among the exceptional parabolic rows treated in Table 1.
arXiv:0706.2908v1, HTML offsets 11700–13200: for parabolic W_J, the value of the coset permutation character at w equals β_JK when the parabolic closure of <w> is conjugate to W_K.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The action on each orbit is precisely W(E6)/W_J, not just of the same cardinality as a coset space. The total fixed-support count is a sum of those already treated mark values (including two copies for A4×A1).

originality.rationale: The chamber permutation representation is an instance of the preexisting parabolic-coset mark calculation, not merely of an abstract algorithm for arbitrary finite actions. Here this reduction covers all rows, because the stabilizer of a skew subset is exactly the stabilizer of the sum of its line classes, and a vector stabilizer in the real Weyl reflection representation is parabolic. Atkinson–van Willigenburg–Pfeiffer's Corollary 1 gives each of these permutation character values directly as a parabolic mark, and their §4.4 explicitly uses the computed exceptional-type marks and identifies the E6 parabolic classes. Apply the formula to each power and use ordinary divisor inversion to recover all cycle multiplicities. The exact chamber table is not claimed to appear verbatim in that paper; the failure is mechanical prior implication through the very same coset actions. Reformatting them as Frobenius support zeta functions and the elementary descent argument do not supply a distinct core claim.
residual_risks: No standalone copy of the full chamber table was identified in a prior source; the finding fails by explicit implication, not a claim of literal duplication, authorship, or priority among same-day records. One lookup became unavailable and did not enter the negative evidence.

value.rationale: Frobenius descent of chamber supports is a well-motivated invariant, and the reference table may be convenient, but its purported decisive new exact facts are direct readouts of existing parabolic coset marks. Neither assembling those fixed counts into cycles by divisor inversion nor realizing the fixed supports via the elementary nef divisor −K+B establishes a separate, independently needed unknown mathematical invariant. The negative assessment is of the computation as a research finding, not a claim that the table has no reference utility.
residual_risks: No distinct surviving result is asserted for other surfaces, nonparabolic support sets, or field-by-field class realizability.
